properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-28 to Eqt Prod Co in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Eqt Prod Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-27
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 885919
Permit API: 063-36924
Unconventional: Yes
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-05-28
Comments: On 5/27/2020 at 1101 hrs., Carey Bell with EQT Production Company called the Department to report a release of approximately 5 to 10 gallons of production fluids and hydraulic oil from a tank at EQT's Diamondville Pad in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. I spoke with Ms. Bell and then with Logan Dominick, EQT's on-site Environmental Coordinator, on 5/27/2020. Mr. Dominick explained the nature of the release and also stated that EQT already had contractors onsite to remediate the release. I explained to Mr. Dominick that rather than conducting an on-site inspection and requesting that all personnel vacate the site (due to current Department Policy regarding COVID-19), I would rather have EQT submit documentation of the release and remediation and I would conduct an administrative inspection. Mr. Dominick supplied this documentation in an email on 5/28/2020 and both the email and attached summary will be uploaded to eFACTS. The following violations are being cited for the release of production fluid and hydraulic oil onto the ground: 78a.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1). These violations are being cited against the most recently drilled well permit number (063-36924), as the ESCGP for this site has been terminated. The release area has been excavated and restored, and the tank has been placed back into service. The above violations will be resolved upon submission of a waste manifest to the Department for the excavated material and inspection of the site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-14 to Dorso Lp in New Stanton Boro, Westmoreland county. CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Dorso Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-14
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 877204
Permit API: 129-26159
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: New Stanton Boro
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to a notification received by the Department from the operator of plugging being conducted at this site. Assisting with this inspection is WQS Eric Norman. Conditions on site are cloudy, light snow on the ground, and approximately 30 degrees. The access road appears rutted with several locations that have standing water present. One such location (Photo 1-3) has what appears to be an outfall basin where two streams meet and then pass under the access road via a culvert heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. It appears that at this location some sediment laden water may have left the road in the vicinity of the hay bales (Photo 1), went down slope and discharged into this basin. At the time of this inspection it does not appear to be currently ongoing. The straw bale barriers at this location do not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. A second location (Photo's 4-7) is actively discharging sediment laden water into WOTC. The water appears to be pooling at a low point on the access road, spilling into a ditch which is conveying through a culvert pipe underneath the access road into a stream heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. A straw bale barrier at this location does not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. The well appears plugged with a monument present with the API number affixed. There is no machinery present on the site. The site does not appear to have been temporarily stabilized and no down slope E&S controls are present. There does not appear to be an E&S Plan on site. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate steps to temporarily stabilize the site to prevent the potential for accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The Department recommends that the operator have E&S Plans prepared by a person trained and experienced in E&S Control methods and techniques applicable to the size and scope of the project and that those plans be on site during all phases of the earth disturbance activity. The Department also recommends that the operator installs downslope controls to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring at the site. An operator representative was spoken to via phone about the conditions on site. Mr. Wagner stated that no E&S Plans had been developed for this project and due to the weather conditions, no efforts were made to stabilize the site against accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Based on this inspection violations are being issued to the operator. The Department requests a timeline and action plan for abating the discharge and possible discharges identified in this inspection. Further violations may be issued based on responses received from the operator.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/18/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Luzerne Township, Fayette county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/18/2026
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8275592
Permit API: 051-22069
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Luzerne Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/18/2026
Comments: On May 18, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4179991.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/20/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 12/20/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plan is on site.- Disturbance along the access road entrance appears to have been regraded at this time (Photos 1-3).- The length of the access road and the well site also appear to have been regraded at this time, including the earthen berm along the access road. - No seed and/or mulch is observed on the regraded access road and site at this time. - The production tank and equipment near and within the earthen berm appear to have been removed from the site (Photo 7). - CFS at the inlet and outlet of the culvert that runs under the access road does not appear to be implemented/maintained properly at this time. - The CFS at the outlet side appears to be overtopping causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation which is observed on the other side of the CFS (Photos 10-13).- Some of the sedimentation observed further downslope in the previous inspection is not visible at this time due to vegetation that appears to have grown on top (Photo 14).- CFS on site does not appear to be implemented/maintained properly at this time (Photos 15-18). The Department recommends the operator chink the CFS.- A section of the slope below the well site is observed to have no CFS below (Photos 19-20). Sediment at the bottom of this section of the slope appears to have been graded/pushed on to piles of brush (Photos 22-25). The Department recommends installing additional CFS where necessary, per the E and S plans. - Well appears to be plugged and buried at this time. Violations remain outstanding for failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, and failure to implement and maintain E and S BMPs.

Comments: On February 1, 2024, inspection conducted at the Athena well pad in Washington Township, Westmoreland County. ESCGP approval was obtained on January 10, 2022 and expires on January 9, 2027. Present were Olympus Energy representative Laura Karosic, independent consultants Brad Latimer and Jeff Leary, and myself. Briefly present was Olympus Energy representative Jim Noon. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that was discovered while removing containment from the pad. The operator reports discovering at least 5 gallons of an oily material on the well pad. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP, PPC plan, ESCGP approval letter, and E and S inspection logs were onsite (see photos 2-4). However, no E and S inspections beyond November 22, 2023 were available in the log onsite. The access road appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The well pad was excavated at the time of inspection to install flow lines to the newly-drilled Utica wells onsite (see photos 6 and 14). A stained area of approximately 65 feet by 55 feet (according to measurements taken by the operator) was observed on the pad (see photos 7-10). Onsite consultants stated that they attempted to dig into the stained gravel in an attempt to gauge how far down the staining goes, but were unable. Ms. Karosic reported conductivity readings below 1,000 Microsiemens in the stained area. She also reported that the well pad drainages were closed-in upon discovery of the stained area. She informed the DEP that sampling will be conducted and remediation will be handled by Moody and Associates within the coming week, and additional information will be provided as additional discoveries are made in their investigation. The operator anticipates to conduct remediation in accordance with Act 2. Because it is unknown when the secondary containment failed, the DEP inquired on the timeline that it was on the pad. The aforementioned representatives informed the DEP that containment was first placed on the pad in late July of 2023 for drilling of the two Utica wells. Additional containment layers and rig mats were placed approximately six months ago for Completions, and the two Utica wells currently await to be fracked. GPU units onsite are equipped with raised secondary containment skids (see photo 13). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 11). The six additional wells onsite that appear to be in production were equipped with well tags, and did not appear to have any evidence of leaks or discharge on the ground around them at the time of inspection (see photo 15). All other containments onsite that appeared to contain regulated substances were placed in secondary containment. PCSM BMP's appeared to be constructed according to the plans onsite. The Department checked the downslope well pad drainages for any evidence of staining or impact from the newly discovered spill. No staining, distressed vegetation, or anything that would substantiate the occurrence of a recent spill was observed (see photos 5 and 18-25). Before departing from site, the DEP spoke with Olympus representative Jim Noon to inform him that the onsite E and S inspection log was incomplete, and that this has also been observed at another Olympus Pad. He stated that Olympus will conduct additional follow up with their EI's and provide them electronically for this site.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued for releasing this unknown oily substance to the surface of the well pad. An additional violation is being issued for threatening the WOTC, as the ground water depth appears to be shallow at approximately 15-200 centimeters in this area according to surveys conducted by the USDA.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/03/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/03/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8227913
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/01/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8206836
Permit API: 113-20463
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Elkland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/01/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of produced fluid from production tanks 2 and 3. It is believed that a malfunctioning ball valve somehow allowed the fluid to escape. The release was discovered around 08:00 on 10/31/24.I initially arrived onsite on 11/1/24. Mountain Energy was onsite cleaning the tanks so they could be moved to excavate the impacted area. The impacted area was already demarcated by Chesapeake. I screened for conductivity within the marked area and got readings between 0.68 to 2.30 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). Beyond the marked area, on the pad and in a rock-lined channel surrounding the pad, the conductivity readings were at or below 0.04 mS/cm. There was no fluid, staining, or other visual impacts noted outside the previously marked area.I returned to the site on 11/4/24. The tanks had been moved and the impacted area had been excavated. The excavation was approximately 30' wide by 35' long and around 10" deep. There was about 1 tri-axle load of material removed and stored on containment. Creston was in the process of collecting Act 2 confirmation samples. Creston's conductivity readings in the marked area after the excavation were at or below 0.5 mS/cm.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). Chesapeake has stated they will pursue remediation through Act 2 and the violations can be closed after that process is completed.

Comments: On 10/23/25 Casey Baldwin, O and G WQS and I were at the Coterra Energy Lauer D. Well Site in Springville Twp., Susquehanna County from 1057 to 1301 hours in response to a well control incident that occurred around 8 AM on 10/22/25. An unknown amount of natural gas and production fluid released out of the 12H well as a result of the well control incident. The weather conditions are overcast skies and chilly with light to moderate west winds, occasional gusts, and temperatures around 50 degrees Fahrenheit. The intent of the inspection is to determine if an impact occurred to the ground surface outside of the Limit of Disturbance (LOD) due to the well control incident.Shortly after arrival we met with Mike Oakley, CHMM, and Environmental Health and Safety Specialist of Coterra and the Coterra contractor Resource Environmental. The Department, Coterra, and Resource walked around the entire perimeter of the well pad and tank pad near the site LOD in a clockwise direction to determine if an impact occurred. We started just west and off the intersection of the site access road and Garrison Road near the Site ID signage. The Department utilized a Hanna Groline HI 98331 Soil Test Meter and an Oakton PCTS 5 meter to perform field conductivity screening of wet soil and small pools of fluid on the surface of the ground off the well pad. Resource utilized a Hanna HI 98192 meter. Conductivity readings do not indicate the release of production fluid has extended off the well pad. See photos for additional details.If you have any questions, do not hesitate to contact me @ 570-346-5533 or jsassi@pa.gov.

Comments: On 02/14/2020 WQS Kristof Eichenlaub conducted incident response inspection # 2999089 On 02/18/2020 at approximately 1350 I conducted a follow up inspection at the site. Foamer product and sediment laden water were discharging from the sediment basin outlet, overwhelming two silt socks, and discharging outside the LOD into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. The discharge caused accelerated erosion below the silt socks and extending into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A contractor for Greylock was utilizing a bucket and a pressurized sprayer bottle in an attempt to remove foamer product from the sediment basin rip rap outlet. I inquired what the contractor was utilizing to eliminate the foam. The contractor informed me they were utilizing fabric softener. I contacted Greylock Regulatory Compliance Coordinator Keith Eighmey via phone, who indicated he was unaware of the contractor's activities. Eighmey indicated Greylock had previously utilized a defoaming agent in the channels and basin to eliminate foamer product. Eighmey indicated Greylock could provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The Department requests Greylock provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The spill had not been remediated and was continuing to discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A sediment laden water discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run was also continuing. Greylock discharged an additional substance to Waters of the Commonwealth during their attempt to remove the foamer. Some violations are ongoing as a result of a spill that was documented on 02/14/2020 (inspection # 2999089). Additional violations of CSL 301 and 307 have occurred due to Greylock discharging a chemical to UNT 8 to reduce the surfactant foam. A violation of OGA3259(2I) has occurred for failure to comply with DEP cleanup order issued on 02/14/2020.

Comments: On site inspection of clean-up of a <30 gallon release of produced fluid (brine water and crude oil) from tanks set on site. Clean stone was brought and piled on site in dump truck to be used to haul out contaminated stone and clay. The mini excavator was used to scrape saturated stone and clay into a pile and load into lined dump truck. The depression left from the clean-up has oily water left in it. Mr. Cochran is going to use a pump and tank to removed remaining water in the depression to be disposed of at a licensed facility. The contaminated stone and clay to be taken to landfill in McKean. The depression left from the clean-up will be backfilled with some type of clean stone material and stone on site. A single layer of rough cut boards were placed as deck of bridge. Dump truck and mini excavator used bridge to access well. Mr. Cochran stated that a second layer of boards will be put down and side rails attached to complete the bridge deck. Gravel to be put on the either side of the bridge.Remaining violations to be lifted when clean-up is completed and bridge repair completed.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-06-26 to Minard Run Oil Co in Jenks Twp, Forest county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Minard Run Oil Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-26
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 854468
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-26
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was on a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed 10-15 feet in the ditch along the access road until it reached the culvert pipe under the access road, it then flowed through the culvert pipe under the road and continued to 300-400 feet through vegetation down grade from the tank battery. A backhoe was brought in at some point after the oil release and a ditch was dug approximately 70-80 feet down grade of the tank battery to contain the oil release. A second ditch was dug approximately 275 feet north and down grade of the first ditch to contain the oil flow already beyond the first ditch. Absorbent pads and loose absorbents were used to collect oil from the atop the water collected in the ditches. The second ditch/trap was set up with drains to allow water to siphon off leaving the oil in containment. Some oil residue was found on the vegetation east of the lower ditch in a connected depression and in the vegetation 10-20 feet north of the ditch/trap. There was no evidence of oil residue beyond these two areas. The oil and water remaining in the secondary containment was removed by a vacuum tanker truck via the discharge pipe, the remaining oil was removed from the leaking tank as well as from the the other tanks on site on Friday, June 21. There were several precipitation events after the oil was released to ground, one on Friday June 21st, the day of the event, another on Monday June 24, the runoff from these events carried the oil down grade to the above mentioned areas. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 550-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Violation ID: 8236732
Permit API: 083-53759
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Foster Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/04/2025
Comments: This follow-up inspection is being conducted to evaluate First America Energy's (FAE) compliance with the October 28, 2024 Consent Order and Agreement (COA) entered into and agreed upon by FAE and the Department. As referenced in the Department's findings under Paragraph G of the COA, a January 3, 2024 inspection with violations (Record No. 3669334) of the Warrant 4917 4917 156 well site and Tank Battery documented evidence of production fluid discharges from the Tank Battery. Elevated specific conductance of standing fluids and soils were observed within the secondary containment area along its western wall, and outside of the secondary containment area beginning at its northern corner.The corrective actions that were agreed to by FAE pertaining to the release of fluids at the Warrant 4917 4917 156 well site and tank battery are outlined under Paragraph 3.b. of the COA.The Department received a written plan from FAE on December 19, 2024. FAE's written plan entails the use of a "mini excavator which will be used to dig small test holes around the release area to determine a perimeter. FAE will determine this parameter by utilizing a probe to test the conductivity of the soil. During this testing, any soil measuring greater than 1,000 micro siemens will be considered contaminated, any soil less than 1,000 micro siemens will be considered clean" (December 19, 2024 written plan). From there, FAE's plan indicates their intention to hire a contractor to remove all soils with elevated specific conductance and backfill the excavated area with native soils.At the time of this inspection, no visual evidence of remediation work can be observed at the Tank Battery. The evidence of production fluid discharge along the western wall of the secondary containment and outside of the secondary containment beginning at its northern corner is visible via areas of no/stressed vegetation, and pooled fluids with elevated specific conductance. Increased deer activity can also be observed in these areas. Pooled fluid atop the affected area within the secondary containment along its western wall was observed to have specific conductance in excess of 1,000 microSiemens per centimeter.There is no evidence of replacement or improvement to the secondary containment, as ordered by Paragraph 3.b.v. of the COA.At the time of this inspection, the Department has not received a Final Report from FAE.

Comments: On 4/13/2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the Holchin 2 well plugging site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 3/16/2026. Tyler Hinkle (Next Level Energy) was on site during this inspection. The following was observed during the inspection:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy representative Tyler Hinkle, who was on site to make minor repairs to the temporary BMPs installed on site and to remove an excavator from site. Hinkle identified during this inspection evidence of third-party disturbance due to livestock grazing on site. The Department recommends that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road and well site. No evidence of accelerated erosion was observed on site during this inspection. The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site. The site appears to be staged for well plugging operations, however no machinery related to well plugging is on site at the time of inspection. The gas well is disconnected from the production equipment. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number was not visible anywhere on site. While on site, the Department reviewed the site E and S/Restoration plans. The Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is not installed in the location shown in the E and S plan drawing (photos 4 and 15). Although an overall BMP layout drawing exists, the plans state that E and S controls are to be installed at contractor's discretion. At the time of this inspection, the E and S controls appear to be installed on site in a manner that is preventing accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring. The Department recommends that that the operator monitor the site and install additional temporary E and S controls as necessary in order to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to occur. The Department recommends that the site E and S/Restoration plans are kept updated via redlining with the BMP's currently installed on site. Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An additional violation shall be issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/09/2021
Comments: On August 9, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response to a spill at EQT COP Tract 551 Pad B. The spill of drilling mud outside of containment was reported on August 6, 2021. The DEP staff met with EQT company man R.D. Mann. Mr. Mann showed the DEP where the spill occurred and explained that a mud line ruptured outside containment. The area had already been excavated and the impacted soil had been removed prior to the inspection. Two ditches were dug to remove the impacted soil and the impacted soil was removed and back filled on the traveling lane of the well pad. The ditch 1 dug was about 20 feet by 3 feet and about 3 feet deep. Ditch 2 was about 15 ft by 4 feet and about 2 feet deep. The estimation of the amount of oil based mud was about 4.2 barrels spilled, not 42 gallons as the detail sheet states. The spill occurred near the sump and french drain that had been dug for a prior release. The DEP recommended vacuuming the water out of Ditch 1 prior to back filling. Another area of the well pad had been scraped to allow water that is leeching from under the secondary containment of the drilling rig to pool and be vacuumed. The water that is leaching from under the containment is from a previously discovered brine spill. The conductivity of the water in the pool was 848 uS/cm. The DEP recommends monitoring the conductivity of the water that becomes pooled. Precision Drilling 110 is onsite and in the process of drilling the fourth well out of nine wells planned for the well pad. Secondary containment berms and liner where it could be observed was in good condition. There were 4 cement silos and 14 baker tanks onsite in secondary containment. The release of drilling mud outside of containment is violation of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Violations remain outstanding from Inspection Report 3207564.
